function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

You fix one issue in a Python repository under `/workspace`. The problem statement is the title and description of the pull request that fixed it, so it usually says what was changed.

You have a limited time and tool-call budget (stated in the task). Every tool call costs time, and writing long text costs far more. Work in this order.

## 1. Locate
- Pull identifiers from the problem statement: function, class, parameter, option name, error text.
- Find them with ONE `run_command` that chains several searches, for example:
  `grep -rn "name_a" --include=*.py . | grep -v -e tests/ -e docs/ | head -15; grep -rn "name_b" --include=*.py . | head -15`
- Then read only the function you need with `read_file`, passing `start_line` and `end_line` (60 lines or fewer). Do not read whole files.

## 2. Edit (as soon as you know where)
- Change the source with `edit_file`: a short `old_string` copied exactly from what you read, and its `new_string`.
- Make the smallest change that does what the problem statement describes.
- An edit on disk is graded even if time runs out. No edit is a certain failure. If you are torn between two fixes, apply the more likely one now and refine it afterwards.

## 3. Check
- Run the closest existing test file once: `python -m pytest tests/test_x.py -x -q 2>&1 | tail -15`
- If it fails because of your change, fix the source. Ignore failures unrelated to your change.

## 4. Submit
- Call `submit_patch`, then reply with one sentence. `submit_patch` ends the session, so call it only when you are done.

## Rules
- Think for a sentence or two before each call. Never plan at length.
- Never create files: no reproduction scripts, no new tests. For a quick check, use `python -c "..."` inside `run_command`. Use `write_file` only when the task itself requires a new source file.
- Never edit tests, `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml` or `setup.cfg`. Those changes are discarded.

function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph

Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

If a Pydantic model has a field with alias `$ref`, Pydantic v2's `model_json_schema()` will put it in the `properties` section of the schema.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:

            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

<|channel>thought
The user wants to fix an issue where using a class (not an instance) as a dependency that has a `__call__` method is not working as expected.

In FastAPI, dependencies are typically functions or classes that are instantiated. If a class has a `__call__` method, it can be used as a callable. However, if the class itself is passed as the dependency, FastAPI might be trying to instantiate it instead of calling it if it's already a callable class.

Wait, if I pass a class `MyDep` to `Depends(MyDep)`, FastAPI normally instantiates `MyDep()`. If `MyDep` has a `__call__` method, `MyDep()` will be an instance of `MyDep`, and that instance can be called. But the problem statement says "using class (not instance) dependency that has `__call__` method".

This suggests that if a class has a `__call__` method, it should be treatable as a dependency directly, or maybe the way FastAPI handles callable classes needs adjustment.

Let's try to reproduce this. I'll create a small script to see what happens.<channel|><|tool_call>call:run_command{command:<|"|>python3 -c "
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

app = FastAPI()

class MyDep:
    def __call__(self):
        return 'hello'

@app.get('/')
def read_root(dep=Depends(MyDep)):
    return dep

client = TestClient(app)
response = client.get('/')
print(f'Response: {response.json()}')
"<|"|>}<tool_call|>

The user is reporting a bug in FastAPI where OpenAPI responses are duplicated when `responses` are defined at the app level with both `model` (as a `Union`) and `content`.
The root cause is identified as a shallow copy of the response dictionary in `fastapi/openapi/utils.py`.

Specifically:
- `additional_response` is taken from `route.responses`.
- It is shallowly copied into `process_response`.
- `process_response['content']` is modified, which in turn modifies `route.responses` because it's a shallow copy.
- Since app-level responses are shared across routes, the modifications accumulate.

I need to fix this by ensuring that the response is deeply copied or that the modifications don't affect the original shared object.

Let's start by locating the code in `fastapi/openapi/utils.py`.<channel|><|tool_call>call:run_command{command:<|"|>grep -rn "process_response" --include=*.py fastapi/openapi/utils.py | head -15<|"|>}<tool_call|>

Specifically, `process_response = additional_response.copy()` is used, but `additional_response['content']` is a dictionary, and shallow copying it means `process_response['content']` and `additional_response['content']` refer to the same object.
When `deep_dict_update` is called on `process_response['content']`, it modifies the original `additional_response['content']` in the `route.responses` object, which is shared across all routes.

I need to change the shallow copy to a deep copy or ensure that `content` is copied properly.

You fix one issue in a Python repository under `/workspace`. The problem statement is the title and description of the pull request that fixed it, so it usually says what was changed.

You have a limited time and tool-call budget (stated in the task). Every tool call costs time, and writing long text costs far more. Work in this order.

## 1. Locate
- Pull identifiers from the problem statement: function, class, parameter, option name, error text.
- Find them with ONE `run_command` that chains several searches, for example:
  `grep -rn "name_a" --include=*.py . | grep -v -e tests/ -e docs/ | head -15; grep -rn "name_b" --include=*.py . | head -15`
- Then read only the function you need with `read_file`, passing `start_line` and `end_line` (60 lines or fewer). Do not read whole files.

## 2. Edit (as soon as you know where)
- Change the source with `edit_file`: a short `old_string` copied exactly from what you read, and its `new_string`.
- Make the smallest change that does what the problem statement describes.
- An edit on disk is graded even if time runs out. No edit is a certain failure. If you are torn between two fixes, apply the more likely one now and refine it afterwards.

## 3. Check
- Run the closest existing test file once: `python -m pytest tests/test_x.py -x -q 2>&1 | tail -15`
- If it fails because of your change, fix the source. Ignore failures unrelated to your change.

## 4. Submit
- Call `submit_patch`, then reply with one sentence. `submit_patch` ends the session, so call it only when you are done.

## Rules
- Think for a sentence or two before each call. Never plan at length.
- Never create files: no reproduction scripts, no new tests. For a quick check, use `python -c "..."` inside `run_command`. Use `write_file` only when the task itself requires a new source file.
- Never edit tests, `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml` or `setup.cfg`. Those changes are discarded.
- Never run the whole test suite and never `pip install`.
- When the fix is in place, or fewer than 5 tool calls remain, submit.

function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph

Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

You have a limited time and tool-call budget (stated in the task). Every tool call costs time, and writing long text costs far more. Work in this order.

## 1. Locate
- Pull identifiers from the problem statement: function, class, parameter, option name, error text.
- Find them with ONE `run_command` that chains several searches, for example:
  `grep -rn "name_a" --include=*.py . | grep -v -e tests/ -e docs/ | head -15; grep -rn "name_b" --include=*.py . | head -15`
- Then read only the function you need with `read_file`, passing `start_line` and `end_line` (60 lines or fewer). Do not read whole files.

- Change the source with `edit_file`: a short `old_string` copied exactly from what you read, and its `new_string`.
- Make the smallest change that does what the problem statement describes.
- An edit on disk is graded even if time runs out. No edit is a certain failure. If you are torn between two fixes, apply the more likely one now and refine it afterwards.

## 3. Check
- Run the closest existing test file once: `python -m pytest tests/test_x.py -x -q 2>&1 | tail -15`
- If it fails because of your change, fix the source. Ignore failures unrelated to your change.

## 4. Submit
- Call `submit_patch`, then reply with one sentence. `submit_patch` ends the session, so call it only when you are done.

## Rules
- Think for a sentence or two before each call. Never plan at length.

- Never run the whole test suite and never `pip install`.

You have a limited time and tool-call budget (stated in the task). Every tool call costs time, and writing long text costs far more. Work in this order.

## 1. Locate

- Find them with ONE `run_command` that chains several searches, for example:

- Then read only the function you need with `read_file`, passing `start_line` and `end_line` (60 lines or fewer). Do not read whole files.

## 2. Edit (as soon as you know where)
- Change the source with `edit_file`: a short `old_string` copied exactly from what you read, and its `new_string`.
- Make the smallest change that does what the problem statement describes.
- An edit on disk is graded even if time runs out. No edit is a certain failure. If you are torn between two fixes, apply the more likely one now and refine it afterwards.

- Run the closest existing test file once: `python -m pytest tests/test_x.py -x -q 2>&1 | tail -15`

- Never run the whole test suite and never `pip install`.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

- Never run the whole test suite and never `pip install`.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

The `Json` type mentioned in the problem statement is likely `pydantic.Json`.

If a user uses `Json[list[str]]`, Pydantic treats it as a string that should be parsed as JSON.

Let's try to reproduce this with a small script.

Okay, so `Json[List[str]]` works fine in Pydantic.

The issue is likely how FastAPI handles it.

If I use it in a FastAPI endpoint:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import Json
from typing import List

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def read_root() -> Json[List[str]]:
    return ["a", "b"]
```

Wait, if the return type is `Json[List[str]]`, Pydantic's `Json` type expects the value to be a string that is a JSON representation of the inner type. But FastAPI usually handles the serialization to JSON automatically.

If I return `["a", "b"]` and the return type is `Json[List[str]]`, Pydantic might try to validate it.

You have a limited time and tool-call budget (stated in the task). Every tool call costs time, and writing long text costs far more. Work in this order.

Forward references in FastAPI are typically handled when resolving type hints for request bodies, query parameters, etc. If a function is wrapped using `functools.wraps`, the original function's metadata (like `__annotations__`) is copied to the wrapper. However, if the wrapper itself is used, FastAPI needs to make sure it can still resolve the forward references from the original function if necessary, or that it handles the wrapped function correctly.

Actually, `functools.wraps` copies `__annotations__` from the wrapped function to the wrapper.

If I have:
```python
def my_func(a: "MyModel"):
    ...

@functools.wraps(my_func)
def wrapper(a):
    return my_func(a)
```
`wrapper.__annotations__` will be `{'a': 'MyModel'}`.

The issue is likely related to how FastAPI resolves these forward references. FastAPI uses `get_type_hints` or a similar mechanism.

            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:

function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph
function.description:
Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

You have a limited time and tool-call budget (stated in the task). Every tool call costs time, and writing long text costs far more. Work in this order.

- Make the smallest change that does what the problem statement describes.

## 3. Check
- Run the closest existing test file once: `python -m pytest tests/test_x.py -x -q 2>&1 | tail -15`
- If it fails because of your change, fix the source. Ignore failures unrelated to your change.

## 4. Submit
- Call `submit_patch`, then reply with one sentence. `submit_patch` ends the session, so call it only when you are done.

## Rules
- Think for a sentence or two before each call. Never plan at length.

function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: get_code_neighbors
function.description:
Discover structural code graph neighbors (callers, callees, definitions) for a given code node.

        Args:
            node: Name of the function, method, or class node (e.g. 'parse_request' or 'app.routes.get_user').
            edge_type: Optional edge relation filter (e.g. 'CALLS', 'DEFINED_IN', 'IMPORTS').
            max_neighbors: Maximum number of neighbor nodes to return (default: 50).

        Returns:
            Dictionary with list of neighbor node names and count.

function.name: search_similar_code
function.description:
Find semantically similar code functions and classes using graph vector embeddings.

        Args:
            query: Function name or code snippet to search for similar implementations.
            k: Number of most similar code nodes to return (default: 10).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing matching node names, code snippets, and similarity scores.

function.name: get_code_subgraph

Extract the relationship graph (nodes and connecting edges) for a focal set of code elements.

        Args:
            nodes: List of function/class node names to include in the induced subgraph.

        Returns:
            Dictionary detailing the subgraph nodes and connecting directed edges.

You have a limited time and tool-call budget (stated in the task). Every tool call costs time, and writing long text costs far more. Work in this order.

## 1. Locate
- Pull identifiers from the problem statement: function, class, parameter, option name, error text.
- Find them with ONE `run_command` that chains several searches, for example:
  `grep -rn "name_a" --include=*.py . | grep -v -e tests/ -e docs/ | head -15; grep -rn "name_b" --include=*.py . | head -15`
- Then read only the function you need with `read_file`, passing `start_line` and `end_line` (60 lines or fewer). Do not read whole files.

## 2. Edit (as soon as you know where)
- Change the source with `edit_file`: a short `old_string` copied exactly from what you read, and its `new_string`.
- Make the smallest change that does what the problem statement describes.
- An edit on disk is graded even if time runs out. No edit is a certain failure. If you are torn between two fixes, apply the more likely one now and refine it afterwards.

## 3. Check
- Run the closest existing test file once: `python -m pytest tests/test_x.py -x -q 2>&1 | tail -15`
- If it fails because of your change, fix the source. Ignore failures unrelated to your change.

## 4. Submit
- Call `submit_patch`, then reply with one sentence. `submit_patch` ends the session, so call it only when you are done.

## Rules
- Think for a sentence or two before each call. Never plan at length.
- Never create files: no reproduction scripts, no new tests. For a quick check, use `python -c "..."` inside `run_command`. Use `write_file` only when the task itself requires a new source file.
- Never edit tests, `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml` or `setup.cfg`. Those changes are discarded.
- Never run the whole test suite and never `pip install`.
- When the fix is in place, or fewer than 5 tool calls remain, submit.

You fix one issue in a Python repository under `/workspace`. The problem statement is the title and description of the pull request that fixed it, so it usually says what was changed.

You have a limited time and tool-call budget (stated in the task). Every tool call costs time, and writing long text costs far more. Work in this order.

## 1. Locate
- Pull identifiers from the problem statement: function, class, parameter, option name, error text.
- Find them with ONE `run_command` that chains several searches, for example:
  `grep -rn "name_a" --include=*.py . | grep -v -e tests/ -e docs/ | head -15; grep -rn "name_b" --include=*.py . | head -15`
- Then read only the function you need with `read_file`, passing `start_line` and `end_line` (60 lines or fewer). Do not read whole files.

## 2. Edit (as soon as you know where)
- Change the source with `edit_file`: a short `old_string` copied exactly from what you read, and its `new_string`.
- Make the smallest change that does what the problem statement describes.
- An edit on disk is graded even if time runs out. No edit is a certain failure. If you are torn between two fixes, apply the more likely one now and refine it afterwards.

## 3. Check
- Run the closest existing test file once: `python -m pytest tests/test_x.py -x -q 2>&1 | tail -15`
- If it fails because of your change, fix the source. Ignore failures unrelated to your change.

## 4. Submit
- Call `submit_patch`, then reply with one sentence. `submit_patch` ends the session, so call it only when you are done.

## Rules
- Think for a sentence or two before each call. Never plan at length.
- Never create files: no reproduction scripts, no new tests. For a quick check, use `python -c "..."` inside `run_command`. Use `write_file` only when the task itself requires a new source file.
- Never edit tests, `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml` or `setup.cfg`. Those changes are discarded.
- Never run the whole test suite and never `pip install`.
- When the fix is in place, or fewer than 5 tool calls remain, submit.

            old_string: Text block to replace.

class _TrackThread(Thread):
    """A thread to periodically update progress."""

    def __init__(self, progress: "Progress", task_id: "TaskID", update_period: float):
        self.progress = progress
        self.task_id = task_id
        self.update_period = update_period
        self.done = Event()

        self.completed = 0
        super().__init__(daemon=True)

    def run(self) -> None:
        task_id = self.task_id
        advance = self.progress.advance
        update_period = self.update_period
        last_completed = 0
        wait = self.done.wait
        while not wait(update_period) and self.progress.live.is_started:
            completed = self.completed
            if last_completed != completed:
                advance(task_id, completed - last_completed)
                last_completed = completed

        self.progress.update(self.task_id, completed=self.completed, refresh=True)

    def __enter__(self) -> "_TrackThread":
        self.start()
        return self

    def __exit__(
        self,
        exc_type: Optional[Type[BaseException]],
        exc_val: Optional[BaseException],
        exc_tb: Optional[TracebackType],
    ) -> None:
        self.done.set()
        self.join()
